newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Western says zinc concentrates up.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Western says zinc concentrates up.

text.p: Western Metals Ltd said on Tuesday its production of zinc concentrates improved in the September quarter despite lower-than anticipated ore head grades.

However, lower lead head grades and difficulty in treating "oily," or high chemical content, ore from its number two pod at the Goongewa deposit in Western Australia left lead concentrate output for the latest quarter below budget, the company said.
Trials were underway to identify a reagent and to determine the extent of the oily ore, Western Metals said.
"The difficult ore is being stockpiled separately and blended with ore from other sources," the company said.

Western metals also said its ore mill at its Cadjebut mine, also in Western Australia, would be shut down between October 15 and October 19 in part to install new equipment to allow for treatment of higher grade lead concentrates expected from the Kapok mine project. Kapok is set to start up in March 1997.

Meanwhile, at Cadjebut, better-than-expected results have been achieved in the latest quarter in the mining of abutments and ore continues to be located in the fringes and floor cleanup, the company said.
Working of Cadjebut, which is nearing the end of its mine life, is expected to continue for the full financial year, ending June 30, Western Metals said.
Overall for the quarter, 27,319 tonnes of zinc concentrate grading 62.3 percent, was produced against 27,972 tonnes at 61.7 percent in the previous quarter, company figures show.
September quarter lead concentrate output totalled 5,779 tonnes at 73.7 percent versus 6,730 tonnes at 78.9 percent in the previous three months.
